title: Clarify and implement model pinning semantics across API and SDK (tag | semver | digest)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define precise semantics for model version pinning supported by the Redwood API and official SDKs. Goal: make pin behavior predictable for production apps and tie published performance profiles to immutable model artifacts. Support three pin forms in a single, consistent syntax: tag (mutable alias), semver (range-aware), and digest/commit hash (immutable). Deliver: API syntax, SDK helpers, server-side resolver, catalog publishing rules, error/fallback UX, and migration guidance.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts model references in the canonical form: '<model-name>@<specifier>' where specifier is one of 'tag:<name>', 'semver:<range>', or 'digest:<sha256>'.
Resolver resolves specifiers to an immutable model digest server-side and returns the digest in response metadata for auditing.
SDKs expose helpers: ModelRef.parse(), ModelRef.pin_by('tag'|'semver'|'digest'), and a --pin-resolve CLI that prints the resolved digest and published perf profile link.
Published performance profiles in the model catalog are bound to digest values; if a tag resolves to a new digest, SDK warns when the digest has changed compared to the last resolved digest.
If a pinned digest is unavailable on a target deployment (region/dedicated pool), request fails with structured 409 and a clear 'fallback' suggestion unless client set allow_fallback=true.
Documentation, migration guide, and at least one end-to-end test covering tag->digest rotation and semver updates are merged.
Security review completed for any metadata signing or KMS usage in catalog publishing.
design_notes: Background: Customers pin models to avoid accidental behaviour changes when a model alias moves. Current platform supports tags and ad-hoc aliasing but semantics are loosely defined across API/SDKs. Proposed canonical syntax: 'my-model@tag:stable' | 'my-model@semver:^1.2.0' | 'my-model@digest:sha256:abcd...'. Server-side behavior: 1) Immediate resolution step map(specifier) -> digest. 2) For tag semantics, tag is a mutable alias that resolves to a digest and carries "published_at" and "publisher" metadata. 3) For semver, the catalog evaluates available releases with semver metadata and picks the highest satisfying digest; the chosen digest recorded. 4) For digest pins, resolution is identity (idempotent). Precedence: If client supplies both a tag and a digest (deprecated form), prefer the explicit digest and emit a deprecation warning. Fallback policy: default: no automatic fallback if digest pinned; optional allow_fallback=true allows falling back to compatible variant (quantized/3-bit) but only if the catalog marks variant as API-compatible and the client explicitly opts in. Performance profiles: only associated with digest. Tag/semver entries include references to the latest digest's profile and a change log. Compatibility scoring: catalog maintains compatibility metadata (api-surface, tokenizer-vocab-hash). SDK UX: resolveModelRef() returns {canonicalName, digest, perfProfileUrl, resolvedAt}. When tag resolution changes (digest drift), SDK emits a non-blocking warning: 'model tag stable moved from <old> to <new> — perf delta +12% latency'.
implementation_plan: Spec PR: add API contract doc and OpenAPI examples (PR #1456)
Server: implement resolver service that maps tag/semver to digest and records resolution events (ENG-7351-a)
Catalog: attach performance-profile artifacts to digest entries; add signed metadata (ENG-7351-b)
SDK: add ModelRef helpers to JS/Python with resolution API call and warning hooks (ENG-7351-c)
API: add response header 'X-Redwood-Model-Digest' and response body metadata 'resolved_digest' for auditability (ENG-7351-d)
Docs: migration guide and examples for typical patterns (pin-by-digest for strict reproducibility; tag for curated "stable"; semver for app-compatible upgrades).
QA: integration tests in staging exercising tag rotation, semver patch upgrades, and digest unavailability cases.
rollout_plan: Staged rollout: 1) Internal dogfooding (redwood-internal org) with SDKs enabled and telemetry for warnings (2 weeks). 2) Canary: 10% of traffic for public API with new header and resolver (3 weeks). 3) Gradual opt-in release: SDK default warning enabled; server accepts new syntax immediately but respects compatibility flag for older clients. 4) After 6 weeks and no critical incidents, flip enforcement for 'pin-by-digest no-fallback' and document breaking change window.
testing_plan: Unit: parser tests for ModelRef.parse() including malformed specifiers and mixed inputs.
Integration: resolve flow using a test catalog with tag rotations and semver variants; assert resolved_digest returned and perf_profile_url matches digest.
E2E: client sets allow_fallback=false and attempts to call a region missing the digest -> expect 409 and structured hint.
Chaos: simulate catalog inconsistency during resolution to exercise retry/backoff behaviors.
Performance: ensure resolution adds <10ms p95 to request path when cached; add cache TTL metrics.
